is_anopheles.evidence: The study focuses on Anopheles gambiae sensu stricto (s.s.) (Page 1, Abstract; Page 2, Methods).

reports_target_markers.evidence: The study screened mosquitoes for kdr East (Vgsc_1014S / L995S) and West (Vgsc_1014F / L995F) mutations (Page 1, Abstract; Page 6, Results).

reports_extractable_genotype_data.evidence: The paper reports that out of 100 samples, 99% had the kdr east mutation and 1% had the kdr west mutation (Page 6), with an overall kdr east allele frequency of 99.14% (Page 8).

african_field_population.evidence: Mosquitoes were collected as wild blood-fed/gravid females from Tulukuyi village, Bungoma County, Kenya, and their F1 progeny were tested (Page 2, Methods).

is_primary_study.evidence: This is a primary empirical study characterizing the microbiota and kdr genotypes of field-collected mosquitoes (Page 2).

sub_country_location.evidence: Collections were conducted in Tulukuyi village, Bungoma County, Kenya, at coordinates 0.56°N 34.56°E (Page 2).

temporal_resolution_within_3y.evidence: Mosquito collections were conducted in April and May 2018 (Page 2).

duplicate_risk.evidence: The samples were collected specifically for this primary microbiota study and there is no indication of overlap with larger genomic databases.

supplement.evidence: The genotype frequencies and sample sizes are sufficiently described in the main text (Page 6 and Page 8).

assessment.summary: This study characterized the microbiota of permethrin-resistant and susceptible Anopheles gambiae s.s. from Tulukuyi village, Bungoma County, Kenya, collected in 2018. It also genotyped 100 of these mosquitoes for Vgsc L995S (kdr-east) and L995F (kdr-west) mutations, finding near-fixation of the L995S mutation (99.14% allele frequency).
